name: Week 10 APT29 and infostealer project evidence
description: Selected APT29/SolarWinds and StellarParticle CTI, checked against ATT&CK v20.1. Colors describe project evidence, not actor confidence or detection coverage. T1059.004 is excluded: the Linux lab is not evidence of APT29 use.

techniques.comment: Trojanized Orion software updates delivered SUNBURST. Delivery-chain context; not executed. Source: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/evasive-attacker-leverages-solarwinds-supply-chain-compromises-with-sunburst-backdoor
PowerShell supported post-compromise commands and task operations. Weeks 5-7 contain historical Windows observations; no fresh Windows run. Source: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/
cmd.exe executed commands on remote machines. Historical cmd control is not validation of remote execution. Source: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/

Existing scheduled tasks were temporarily modified, then restored. Week 8 planned persistence; not executed in Week 9. Source: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/evasive-attacker-leverages-solarwinds-supply-chain-compromises-with-sunburst-backdoor

RDP Bitmap Cache reconstruction showed a Chrome export of saved passwords to plaintext CSV (CrowdStrike figure 4). Mock JSON is not a browser credential store or DPAPI validation. Source: https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/observations-from-the-stellarparticle-campaign/

Shellbags showed Chrome and DPAPI directory navigation. Falcon identified the Cookie Editor extension used in the reported session reuse (figures 2–3). Fake cookies were archived; no valid session or cookie theft was tested. Source: https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/observations-from-the-stellarparticle-campaign/
Files were extracted from compromised networks. Only generated lab files were read; no general collection detector. Source: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/

7-Zip created password-protected archives, sometimes split into parts. Week 9 executed Linux tar/gzip on mock files; this is a portable behavior analogue. Source: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2021/01/20/deep-dive-into-the-solorigate-second-stage-activation-from-sunburst-to-teardrop-and-raindrop/
Archives were staged on a victim OWA server. Local out/ artifacts do not demonstrate remote staging. Source: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/
An HTTPS request retrieved an archive staged on the victim OWA server. No exfiltration was executed; an archive alone proves no data transfer. Source: https://attack.mitre.org/campaigns/C0024/
